reasoning: Recent Montana polling and coverage over the last few weeks consistently show Republican Kurt Alme leading the open U.S. Senate race by high single- to mid–double-digit margins against Democrat Alani Bankhead and independent Seth Bodnar, with no credible, state-specific general-election presidential polling in this window. In multi-candidate general-election trial heats, Alme is typically in the mid-40s to high-40s while his opponents divide the anti-Republican vote in the 20s or low 30s, producing Republican leads in the roughly R+12 to R+17 range, so the current evidence points to an **R+15±3** environment for the Montana Senate race rather than any discernible presidential margin. Structurally, Montana’s Cook PVI remains strongly Republican (about R+11 statewide), reinforcing the GOP edge suggested by these polls and predictive markets.

sources.name: Oddsshopper summary of Tavern Research Montana Senate poll
sources.details: Tavern Research Democratic-firm poll of 517 likely voters found Kurt Alme at 49%, Bodnar 25%, Bankhead 24%, and Austin 2% in the full U.S. Senate field, a 24-point lead over Bodnar and 25 over Bankhead that illustrates a dominant Republican position.

sources.name: Forward Montana / Hart Research Montana Senate poll

sources.name: Washington Reporter writeup of NRSC Montana Senate poll
sources.details: An NRSC-commissioned poll obtained by Washington Reporter showed Alme leading a three-way Senate race 45% to Bankhead’s 30% and Bodnar’s 15%, and also ahead in head-to-head matchups, including 50–43 against Bodnar and 49–46 against Bankhead.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice July 2026 Montana Senate survey
sources.details: Independent Center Voice’s benchmark survey of 793 likely Montana voters found Alme leading the open U.S. Senate race, with Bodnar narrowly outperforming Bankhead for second place, indicating a clear Republican advantage even in a multi-candidate environment.

sources.name: Polling USA summary of Bullfinch Montana Senate poll
sources.details: Bullfinch poll as summarized by Polling USA found Alme at 36%, Bodnar 24%, and Bankhead 22% in the Montana U.S. Senate race, giving the Republican a 12-point lead over Bodnar and 14 points over Bankhead.

sources.details: Race to the WH polling aggregation, as cited by OddsShopper, shows Alme at 44.0%, Bodnar 27.5%, Bankhead 18.9% with 9.6% undecided, for roughly a 16.5-point lead for the Republican in the Montana Senate race.

sources.details: OddsShopper’s analysis of prediction markets notes Kalshi pricing a Republican win in the Montana Senate race at around 90 cents, implying roughly a 90% chance for Alme and describing the race as one he is overwhelmingly likely to win.

sources.name: Flathead Beacon coverage of Montana Senate polling and field-clearing efforts
sources.details: Flathead Beacon reports that internal and public polling shows Bodnar and Bankhead roughly splitting 45–49% of the vote between them with Alme hovering just above 40%, characterizing the Republican as holding the lead while Democrats and independents divide the rest.

sources.name: The Atlantic article on Democratic strategy backfiring in Montana Senate race
sources.details: The Atlantic notes that recent Republican and Democratic polling shows Bodnar and Bankhead splitting the non-Alme vote in a four-way race, leaving Alme with a significant double-digit lead in the Montana Senate contest.

sources.name: Daily Montanan analysis of Montana Senate race competitiveness
sources.details: Daily Montanan reports that available polling shows Alme winning comfortably in any three- or four-way Senate scenario, while only a two-way race against Bodnar is described as more competitive, reinforcing the narrative of a favored Republican.

sources.name: Montana Free Press discussion of withdrawal pressure in Montana Senate race
sources.details: Montana Free Press notes pressure on Bodnar and Bankhead to withdraw before the August 10 deadline and cites Washington Reporter polling with Alme at 45%, Bankhead 30%, Bodnar 15%, suggesting that any multi-candidate ballot configuration siphons votes from the non-Alme side.

sources.name: Montana Public Radio coverage of finalized Montana Senate ballot
sources.details: Montana Public Radio reports that both Bankhead and Bodnar remained on the ballot past the withdrawal deadline, locking in a three-way general-election Senate race widely expected to advantage Alme by splitting the anti-Republican vote.
